acceptance_rules.A1_search: Expected section in the top 15 for at least 4 of 5 questions, in each of 3 routed runs.

cases.question: My brother was arrested after the police found drugs in a bag inside a shared apartment in Bengaluru. Several people had access to that room, but the police are blaming him. What legal rights does he have, and how can he challenge the allegation?
cases.why: NDPS s.35 presumption of culpable mental state, but 'it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that he had no such mental state'; s.54 presumption from possession 'unless and until the contrary is proved'; s.52(1) the arresting officer shall 'inform him of the grounds for such arrest'; BNSS s.47 person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail; s.48 inform a relative or friend.
cases.author: project owner

cases.question: The police searched my rented room in Kolkata and seized some suspected narcotic substances. They didn't explain why they were searching the room. What legal safeguards apply during a search and seizure under the NDPS Act?
cases.why: s.42 entry/search without warrant only by an empowered officer who 'has reason to believe from personal knowledge or information given by any person and taken down in writing'; s.41 warrant/authorisation; s.50 a person about to be searched may require to be taken to the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate; s.52 grounds of arrest.
cases.author: project owner

cases.question: Someone was arrested in Mumbai with a large quantity of an illegal drug in their car. The police are accusing him of drug trafficking. How does Indian law distinguish small, intermediate and commercial quantities?
cases.why: s.2(xxiiia) 'small quantity' means any quantity lesser than the quantity specified by the Central Government by notification; s.2(viia) 'commercial quantity' greater than the notified quantity; ss.20-22 set different punishments for small, intermediate and commercial quantity; s.37 bail limits for commercial quantity.
cases.also_check: Must say the exact quantities are set by notification and not state grams.
cases.author: project owner

cases.question: The police caught my friend smoking cannabis at a private gathering in Delhi. He wasn't selling anything or carrying a large quantity. Can he still be arrested, and what punishment does the law provide?
cases.why: s.27 punishment for consumption of any narcotic drug; s.20 cannabis; s.64A immunity from prosecution for an addict charged under s.27 or small quantity who voluntarily seeks de-addiction treatment; s.39 probation.
cases.author: project owner

cases.question: I was caught by the police in possession of a small amount of ganja while travelling in Assam. I've never been involved in anything like this before. What legal consequences could I face?
cases.why: s.20 cannabis, with a separate punishment where the contravention involves small quantity; s.2 'ganja' within cannabis (hemp) and 'small quantity' by notification; s.39 probation for small quantity offenders; s.64A immunity for addicts seeking treatment.
cases.author: project owner
